resources.string: Civic Monitor runs a custom-trained YOLO11n model entirely on this device to spot 16 street-level conditions in real time: garbage piles, potholes, encroachments, unauthorized billboards, manholes (closed, open or broken), streetlights (working or not working), and stray animals on the road — cow, buffalo, goat, horse, dog, cat and camel. Manhole and streetlight state is now predicted directly by the model rather than inferred, and works in daylight as well as at night. Healthy states are shown on screen but never filed as incidents. No footage or images leave the phone for detection — everything runs offline, on-device. Each confirmed issue is saved locally as a photo plus a JSON report (class, confidence, timestamp, camera ID).

• GPS auto-tagging — attach live latitude/longitude to every incident automatically

• Cloud sync queue — upload saved reports to a municipal dashboard whenever Wi-Fi/data is available, fully offline-first otherwise

• Severity scoring — combine confidence + bounding-box size to prioritize the worst potholes/garbage piles first

• Duplicate suppression — use GPS + class to avoid re-reporting the same pothole every time a camera passes it

• Web dashboard for authorities — map view of all incidents, filterable by ward, category, and resolved/open status

• Grievance portal integration — auto-file complaints into existing government systems (e.g. Swachhata App, PGPortal)

• Before/after verification — mark an incident resolved with a follow-up photo once repaired

• Fleet mode — run across multiple municipal vehicles or fixed CCTV poles, aggregated centrally by camera ID

• OTA model updates — download improved detection models periodically without reinstalling the app

• Multilingual UI — Hindi and regional-language support

• Citizen reporting mode — let residents submit their own photos alongside automated detections

• Battery-aware throttling — reduce inference rate automatically on low battery or when the phone is heating up
